correctness.rationale: For k,m>=2, omitted two same-blade vertices are true twins with identical distances to all landmarks, establishing necessity. Conversely each blade supplies >=m-1>=1 selected vertex, and at least two blades are present. Every same-blade pair has different distance differences from a selected endpoint and another blade; a cross-blade pair is separated by one selected vertex from each blade with opposite-sign differences; center–blade pairs are separated using the blade and a different blade. The center may be chosen or omitted. Independent multiplication of m choices of omission or full blade and optional center gives (1+z)(m*z^(m-1)+z^m)^k, min degree k(m-1), and m^k minimum sets. Excluded k=1 and m=1 boundaries do have counterexamples. An independent BFS-based program exhaustively checked 9 parameter pairs, 20768 vertex subsets, every polynomial coefficient, and both excluded boundary counterexamples. These finite checks corroborate, not prove, unbounded k,m.

evidence: Nie–Xu (2024) Lemma 5.1(ii): a doubly resolving set of a noncomplete block graph omits at most one non-cut vertex per nontrivial block; Lemma 5.3 constructs a doubly resolving set by deleting one arbitrarily chosen non-cut vertex per nontrivial block; Theorem 5.4 states psi(G)=leaves(G)+zeta(G)-q(G). The source proof in Section 5 verifies the construction.
Theorem 5.4 covers ALL noncomplete block graphs; generalized windmills with k,m>=2 are one subfamily. Lemma 5.3 supplies actual all-choices minimum sets, not just a numerical minimum.
broader_coverage.reasoning: W_{k,m} is a noncomplete block graph with k nontrivial blocks K_{m+1}, all sharing only the cut vertex c, km non-cut vertices, no leaves, and q=k. Lemma 5.1(ii) forces at most one omission from each peripheral clique. For any choices of one omitted vertex per clique, Lemma 5.3 constructs the exactly corresponding doubly resolving set; every superset stays doubly resolving. Consequently the full iff statement is a direct specialization, not a new converse. Theorem 5.4 gives psi=km-k. Counting each blade (m choices of exactly m-1 vertices or all m vertices) and the optional center yields (1+z)(m z^{m-1}+z^m)^k and m^k minimum sets. Therefore the entire proposed polynomial and basis classification are mechanically implied by the 2024 work, despite not being written there in that exact notation.

originality.rationale: FAIL: The claim is already a direct special case/corollary of Nie and Xu (2024), Lemmas 5.1(ii), 5.3, Theorem 5.4 on ALL noncomplete block graphs. W_{k,m} is a block graph with exactly k nontrivial clique blocks, km non-cut vertices and no leaves. Theorem 5.4 yields psi=k(m-1). Lemma 5.1 gives necessary <=1 omission per blade; the construction and its proof in Lemma 5.3 allow any omitted vertex per block, giving sufficiency; upward closure gives ALL permitted S. The whole polynomial and m^k minimum count are then a routine independent product count. Prior coverage is decisive even though exact generating polynomial is not printed in the prior paper.
residual_risks: No meaningful originality residual can overcome the direct 2024 theorem/lemma implication; exact prior enumerator typography was not located but is unnecessary.
